@graph.description: Independent studio for creators across music, art, writing and film. Talent architecture and artist development.
knowsAbout: Multidisciplinary Artist & Repertoire (A&R) across music, visual art, literature, and film

itemOffered.name: Sovereign A&R
itemOffered.description: Multidisciplinary Artist & Repertoire: scouting artists and developing complete bodies of work across music, visual art, literature, and film through critique, direction, and critical framing. The artist retains 100% ownership and creative control. Wild-Lake takes 0% IP ownership and 0% revenue share.

@graph.name: Argelys Samuel Oriach

alumniOf.name: Northwestern University’s National High School Institute (Cherubs) theatre program

@graph.description: Argelys Samuel Oriach is a Dominican-born performance artist, artistic director, and systems architect based in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. He is the founder and artistic director of Wild Lake Studio. He constructs systems and inhabits them. Performance governs his practice, and writing, voice, movement, design, and corporate roles are its forms. He operates two laboratories: Seven Eighty Three (Lab 783), an independent systems design practice, and Wild Lake Studio, its research laboratory, which guides developing and independent artists.

subjectOf.name: Breaking the circle of the plantation: Violence, affect and the ephemeral in Junot Díaz’s Afro-Caribbean literary imagination
subjectOf.description: The thesis positions The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao as an alternative archive of the diaspora. It examines Díaz's Afro-Caribbean literary imagination through queer theory, performance studies, affect studies, and critical race theory.
